verdict.rationale: EFTPS documents mandatory sign-in MFA through the credential providers Login.gov and ID.me, which an authorized human can complete remotely (eftps-supp-1, eftps-docs-14). However, the published enrollment path ends with a PIN sent by U.S. Mail in five to seven business days (eftps-supp-2). That is exactly the physical-mail PIN wall the story rules out, so the full sign-in path is not purely remote credential MFA. Missing for 10: a fully remote enrollment-to-sign-in path with no mailed PIN, and documentation of whether the Login.gov/ID.me identity proofing avoids biometric liveness or in-person steps.
